output.reason: Sudden, painless, persistent monocular vision loss two hours ago in a 55-year-old is a possible central retinal artery occlusion or retinal detachment, both time-critical and requiring immediate emergency eye and stroke assessment.
output.patientMessage: Go to the emergency department now. Sudden painless loss of vision in one eye that hasn't returned can be a blocked retinal artery — treated as a stroke of the eye — or a detached retina, and both need same-hour examination and imaging. Do not drive yourself; have someone take you or call 911. If you develop face droop, weakness, numbness or speech trouble, call 911 immediately.
differential: Retinal detachment or vitreous/retinal vascular cause
